  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Onion (1 large)
  • Cilantro (2 tablespoons)
  • Mustard oil (1 tablespoon)
  • Salt (to taste)

Method

First, wash the tomatoes, dice them, and put them in a pan over the heat. Cook until fully softened — within a few minutes all the tomatoes will break down. Mash any large pieces with a spatula. When the tomato juices have reduced, transfer to a bowl.

In the bowl, add diced onion, chopped cilantro, diced green chilies, mustard oil, and salt, and mash together well. Combine thoroughly with the cooked tomatoes and serve.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Malabar Spinach and Prawns
item.description: A simple but delicious malabar spinach and prawn curry
item.content:encoded:
Malabar spinach with prawns is one of my favorite curries. Here is the recipe.

Ingredients

  • Malabar spinach (500 g)
  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Onion (1)
  • Turmeric powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Prawns (20–25)
  • Salt (to taste)

Method

First, wash the malabar spinach well and cut it as needed. You can halve any large leaves down the middle. Dust the prawns with a pinch of turmeric and shallow-fry them lightly in oil. Heat oil in a pot and add chopped onion. Then add turmeric powder, chili powder, and salt. Add the malabar spinach with a little water and cover. The greens will wilt and shrink quickly. Add the fried prawns and green chilies, stir for 2–3 minutes, and serve.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Bottle Gourd Dal
item.description: An easy recipe for dal cooked with bottle gourd
item.content:encoded:
Bottle gourd is in season now. Here is how to cook dal with it.

Ingredients

  • Lentils (1/2 cup)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Small bottle gourd (1)
  • Onion (1)
  • Garlic (1–2 cloves)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Green chilies (1–2)
  • Cilantro (to taste)
  • Oil (2 tablespoons)

Method

Peel the bottle gourd, cut it into small pieces, and boil until tender. Drain and set aside in a bowl.

In a pot, boil the washed lentils in enough water. Add 1 teaspoon of turmeric. When the lentils are cooked, season with salt and add the boiled bottle gourd and green chilies. Take the pot off the heat once the gourd is well mixed into the dal.

Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan and fry the chopped onion and garlic until golden. Pour the oil and fried aromatics into the cooked dal. Simmer for another 1–2 minutes. Add chopped cilantro just before serving.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Egg and Potato Curry
item.description: An easy recipe for a distinctively flavored egg and potato curry
item.content:encoded:
I have loved eggs since I was little. My mother used to make this special egg and potato curry for me. Here is the recipe.

Ingredients

  • Eggs (3)
  • Potatoes (3–4)
  • Tomato (1)
  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Onion (1)
  • Turmeric powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Salt (to taste)

Method

First, dice the potatoes and wash them. Wash one tomato and cut it into cubes.

Beat 3 eggs with some chopped onion and green chili to make an omelet mixture. Cook the omelet over low heat in a wide pan. When it is partly set, fold it like a patisapta pitha and fry until done.

Heat oil in a pot and add the remaining chopped onion. Then add turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Add the potatoes and tomato, along with enough water to cook. Cover the pot.

The potatoes will soften in a few minutes. Add the fried egg and green chilies. Stir for 2–3 minutes, then take the curry off the heat.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Tomato Tok
item.description: A classic Bengali tomato tok recipe
item.content:encoded:
Tomato tok is an easy and delicious dish. Here is the recipe.

Ingredients

  • Tomatoes (5–6)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Onion (1)
  • Garlic (1–2 cloves)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Green chilies (1–2)
  • Cilantro (to taste)
  • Oil (2 tablespoons)

Method

Wash the tomatoes and cut them into large cubes. Boil them in enough water until soft. Mash the tomatoes into the cooking liquid with a ladle or wooden spoon. Add a little turmeric, then salt and green chilies to taste. Remove from the heat when it reaches your preferred thickness.

Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan and fry the chopped onion and garlic until golden. Pour the oil and fried aromatics into the cooked tomatoes. Simmer for another 1–2 minutes. Add chopped cilantro just before serving.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Dried Chili Mash
item.description: A mouth-watering dried chili mash recipe
item.content:encoded:
For those who love spicy food, the very name of dried chili mash makes the mouth water. Here is a very easy recipe.

Ingredients

  • Dried chilies (8–10)
  • Onion (1 large)
  • Cilantro (2 tablespoons)
  • Mustard oil (1 tablespoon)
  • Salt (to taste)

Method

First, fry the dried chilies in oil until crisp. In a bowl, combine diced onion, chopped cilantro, and the fried dried chilies with salt, and mash everything together well. Add mustard oil and mash once more before serving.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Cucumber and Prawn Curry
item.description: An easy recipe for cucumber, potato, and prawn curry
item.content:encoded:
Here is a recipe for a simple but incredibly delicious cucumber and prawn curry.

Ingredients

  • Cucumber (2 large)
  • Potato (2)
  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Onion (1)
  • Turmeric powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Prawns (20–25)
  • Salt (to taste)

Method

First, peel the cucumber and cut away the soft core with the seeds. Cut the rest into small cubes. Peel the potatoes, cube them, and wash both vegetables together. Dust the prawns with a pinch of turmeric and shallow-fry them lightly in oil.

Heat oil in a pot and add chopped onion. Then add turmeric powder, chili powder, and salt. Add the potato and cucumber, pour in enough water, and cover. The potato and cucumber will soften quickly. Add the fried prawns and green chilies, stir for 2–3 minutes, and take off the heat.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Bhuna Khichuri Recipe
item.description: An easy bhuna khichuri recipe
item.content:encoded:
Bhuna khichuri is one of my absolute favorites. Here is the recipe.

Ingredients

  • Polao rice (2 cups)
  • Red lentils (1/2 cup)
  • Roasted mung dal (1/2 cup)
  • Water (6 cups)
  • Green chilies (4–5)
  • Onion (1)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Cumin powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Coriander powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Ginger-garlic paste (1 teaspoon)
  • Oil (1 tablespoon)
  • Salt (to taste)

Method

Wash the rice and dal mixture and drain. Heat oil in a pot and add chopped onion. When the onion softens, add all the spices and keep stirring until well fried.

Add the rice-dal mixture and fry well. When toasted, add water. Use twice as much water as the total rice and dal. When the water has mostly reduced, add green chilies. Cover and let it steam on very low heat for about 10 minutes. Serve hot.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Watermelon Rind Payesh
item.description: A recipe for payesh made with watermelon rind
item.content:encoded:
I love watermelon. Here is an unusual recipe for payesh made with watermelon rind.

Ingredients

  • Chopped watermelon rind (1 cup)
  • Sugar (1 cup)
  • Milk (1/2 liter)
  • Cardamom (2–3)
  • Cinnamon (2–3 sticks)
  • Bay leaf (1)
  • Ghee (2 tablespoons)
  • Raisins (for serving)

Method

First, remove the green outer skin from the watermelon rind. Chop the white part very finely and boil it briefly in a little water. Drain well.

Heat ghee in a pot and add the cardamom, cinnamon, and bay leaf. Add the boiled watermelon rind and fry it well. Then add the sugar and milk. When the milk has thickened, remove from the heat. Serve sprinkled with raisins.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Vegetable Khichuri Recipe
item.description: An easy vegetable khichuri recipe
item.content:encoded:
Here is an easy vegetable khichuri recipe.

Ingredients

  • Rice (2 cups)
  • Red lentils (1/2 cup)
  • Roasted mung dal (1/2 cup)
  • Water (6 cups)
  • Green chilies (4–5)
  • Onion (1)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Oil (1 tablespoon)
  • Tomato (1)
  • Potato (1)
  • Carrot (1)
  • Spinach (1 cup)
  • Zucchini (1/2 cup)
  • Cauliflower (2–3 florets)
  • Broccoli (2–3 florets)
  • Salt (to taste)

Method

Wash the rice and dal mixture and drain. Heat oil in a pot and add chopped onion. When the onion softens, add all the spices and keep stirring. Then add all the vegetables and cook until well fried. Add the rice and dal and cook a little longer.

Add water and cover. When the water has absorbed, add a few green chilies, cover for 2–3 minutes, and serve hot.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Canned Tuna Mash
item.description: Canned tuna mash recipe
item.content:encoded:
Back home I loved takki fish mash, but fresh takki is hard to find here. Tuna is widely available, so wherever you are, here is a tuna mash recipe.

Ingredients

  • Canned tuna (1 can — 190 grams)
  • Onion (1)
  • Dried chilies (4–5)
  • Mustard oil (to taste)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Cilantro (to taste)

Method

First, drain the tuna from the can and squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Heat a little oil in a pan and fry the tuna for 2–3 minutes. A light fry is enough — it removes the raw fish smell.

Lightly fry diced onion in the pan. You can also use raw onion for this mash if you prefer. Fry the dried chilies as well. In a bowl, mash together onion, dried chilies, cilantro, and salt. Add mustard oil to taste and the tuna, and mash until well combined.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Hilsa Jhal Kosha
item.description: A recipe for spicy hilsa kosha with kaffir lime leaves
item.content:encoded:
Hilsa is a favorite for all of us. Here is a distinctive recipe made with hilsa fish.

Ingredients

  • Hilsa fish (1 medium)
  • Chopped onion (1 cup)
  • Turmeric powder (2 teaspoons)
  • Chili powder (2 teaspoons)
  • Ginger paste (1 teaspoon)
  • Garlic paste (1 teaspoon)
  • Green chilies (5–6)
  • Kaffir lime leaves (3–4)
  • Salt (to taste)

Method

First, cut and wash the hilsa, rub lightly with salt and turmeric, fry, and set aside.

Heat oil in a pot and add chopped onion. When the onion softens, add all the spices except the kaffir lime leaves and green chilies, and fry, adding a little water if needed so nothing burns. When the spices are ready, add the hilsa and whole green chilies. Cook for 5–7 minutes. One or two minutes before taking the pot off the heat, add the kaffir lime leaves. Serve hot.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Tomato Salmon Curry
item.description: A Bengali-style salmon curry with tomato and potato
item.content:encoded:
Salmon is easy to find in grocery stores across Europe and America, and even in supermarkets back home. Here is a Bengali-style salmon curry with tomato and potato.

Ingredients

  • Salmon fillets (2 pieces, 250 g)
  • Tomato (3)
  • Potato (2)
  • Onion (1)
  • Turmeric powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Cilantro (for serving)

Method

First, wash the salmon fillets, rub lightly with turmeric, shallow-fry in oil, and set aside.

Heat oil in a pot and add chopped onion. When the onion softens, add turmeric powder, chili powder, and salt. Add medium-sized cubed tomato and long potato slices. Stir lightly and add 1 cup water. The potato will soften quickly and the tomato will break down into a coating gravy. Add the fried fish and green chilies and cook 2–3 minutes more.

Finish with cilantro and serve.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Khichuri Recipe
item.description: An easy khichuri recipe made in a rice cooker
item.content:encoded:
We all love khichuri. Here is how to cook it in a rice cooker.

Ingredients

  • Rice (1 cup)
  • Red lentils (1/4 cup)
  • Roasted mung dal (1/4 cup)
  • Water (3 cups)
  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Onion (1)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Oil (1 tablespoon)
  • Tomato (1)
  • Potato (1)

Method

Wash the potato and tomato and cut them into small cubes. Add all the ingredients except water to the rice cooker and mix well. I used 1 cup rice and 1/2 cup of two types of dal. You can use any one type of dal if you prefer. Use twice as much water as the total rice and dal combined. For 1.5 cups of rice and dal, I used 3 cups of water. Turn on the rice cooker. When it switches from cook to warm, the khichuri is ready. Serve hot.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Eggplant Mash
item.description: Eggplant mash made in the microwave recipe
item.content:encoded:
Eggplant mash is one of my favorite dishes. Back home I could roast it over an open flame, but that is not an option here — so here is how to make it in the microwave.

Ingredients

  • Large round eggplant (1)
  • Dried chilies (2–3)
  • Onion (1)
  • Mustard oil (to taste)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Cilantro (to taste)

Method

First, remove the stem from the eggplant, wash it, and score it a few times with a knife. Rub with a little mustard oil and microwave for 12–15 minutes. When the eggplant is soft, take it out. If water has collected at the bottom of the dish, discard it. Mash while still hot.

Add diced onion, chopped cilantro, fried dried chilies, salt, and mustard oil, and mash until well combined. Serve hot with rice or khichuri.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Laccha Semai
item.description: An easy recipe for laccha semai
item.content:encoded:
No festival, including Eid, feels complete without semai. Here is a recipe for laccha semai.

Ingredients

  • Laccha semai (250 g)
  • Milk (1 liter)
  • Sugar (1 cup)
  • Cardamom (2)
  • Cinnamon (2 sticks)
  • Bay leaf (1)
  • Raisins (for serving)
  • Cashews (for serving)

Method

First, in the dish you will serve the semai in, lightly break apart the laccha semai from the packet and arrange it. In a pot, heat the milk with the sugar, cardamom, cinnamon, and bay leaf. When it comes to a boil, pour the milk over the laccha semai and sprinkle chopped raisins and cashews on top. The amount of milk may seem like a lot, but within a few minutes the semai will absorb it all. Serve once it has cooled slightly.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Shahi Tukra
item.description: A recipe for Dhaka's traditional dessert, shahi tukra
item.content:encoded:
Here is how to make shahi tukra.

Ingredients

  • Bread (5–6 slices)
  • Full-fat milk (1 kg)
  • Condensed milk (250 g)
  • Sugar (2 cups)
  • Raisins (1 tablespoon)
  • Chopped nuts (2 tablespoons)
  • Ghee (for frying the bread)
  • Cardamom (2)
  • Cinnamon (2 sticks)
  • Bay leaf (1)

Method

First, trim the crusts from the bread slices and cut them into small triangles. Lightly fry them in ghee and set aside. Arrange them neatly in the dish you will use for the shahi tukra.

In a pot, heat the milk, condensed milk, and sugar with the cardamom, cinnamon, and bay leaf, stirring constantly until the milk reduces by about half. Pour the milk over the fried bread and sprinkle chopped nuts and raisins on top. Once the milk has cooled to room temperature, refrigerate it. Shahi tukra is usually served cold. Take it out of the fridge before serving.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Dorado Fish Dopeyaja
item.description: A recipe for dorado fish dopeyaja with tomato
item.content:encoded:
Bengalis are crazy about fish. Those of us living abroad surely miss fresh fish the way I do. Local fish is available frozen at Bangladeshi shops, but fresh fish usually means local varieties. Here is how to cook dorado fish dopeyaja in a Bengali style.

Ingredients

  • Dorado fish (1 medium)
  • Tomato (3–4)
  • Onion (1 cup)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Scallions (for serving)
  • Cilantro (for serving)

Method

First, scale and wash the fish, cut it into pieces, rub lightly with turmeric, and shallow-fry. Dorado cooks quickly, so 1–2 minutes of frying is enough.

Heat oil in a pan and add chopped onion. When the onion softens, add diced tomato, turmeric, chili powder, and salt, and fry the spices until the tomato breaks down. Add the fried fish and cook for about five minutes. Just before serving, scatter chopped scallions and cilantro on top.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Beef Haleem
item.description: A recipe for beef haleem made with Radhuni haleem mix
item.content:encoded:
We all love haleem. Here is an easy recipe using haleem mix and beef.

Ingredients

  • Radhuni haleem mix (1 packet)
  • Chopped onion (1 cup)
  • Beef (500 g)
  • Ginger paste (1 teaspoon)
  • Garlic paste (1 teaspoon)
  • Green cardamom (3)
  • Oil (1 cup)
  • Cinnamon (3 pieces)
  • Cloves (3)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Julienned ginger (for serving)
  • Chopped green chilies (for serving)
  • Chopped cucumber (for serving)
  • Lemon (for serving)

Method

Pour the grain packet from the Radhuni haleem mix into a bowl and soak in water for 30 minutes to 1 hour. In another pot, fry some of the chopped onion in oil until golden and crispy. Set the fried onions aside.

Wash 500 g beef and marinate it with the spice packet from the haleem mix, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, ginger paste, garlic paste, and salt. Let it rest for 15 minutes. In a large pot, heat oil and fry the remaining onion until lightly browned. Add the marinated beef and cook, stirring, until the meat is tender. Add water as needed so the spices do not burn.

Once the meat is cooked, add the soaked grains and cook until they are tender. Keep cooking until the haleem reaches your preferred thickness.

Serve hot topped with julienned ginger, chopped cucumber, green chilies, fried onions, and a wedge of lemon.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Puffed Rice Balls (Muri Moya)
item.description: A recipe for the beloved Bengali snack muri moya
item.content:encoded:
Muri moya brings back childhood memories of buying moya from an old glass jar. Here is how to make it easily at home.

Ingredients

  • Puffed rice (muri) (500 g)
  • Sugar or jaggery (500 g)
  • Green cardamom (2)
  • Cinnamon (2 pieces)
  • Bay leaf (1)

Method

Sift 500 g puffed rice through a strainer to remove dust, sand, and broken bits. In a large pot, make a syrup with the jaggery or sugar and a little water — I usually use 1 cup water for 500 g jaggery. Add the cardamom, cinnamon, and bay leaf for a lovely aroma.

When the syrup is nearly ready, remove the whole spices and take the pot off the heat. Immediately add the puffed rice and mix well. While the mixture is still warm — before the syrup sets — shape it into balls.

Store in an airtight container and enjoy for a long time.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Pancakes
item.description: Make soft, delicious pancakes for breakfast in a few simple steps
item.content:encoded:
Pancakes are hard to beat for breakfast. Here is a simple recipe.

Ingredients

  • All-purpose flour (1 cup)
  • Butter (1 tablespoon)
  • Egg (1)
  • Milk (1 cup)
  • Sugar (2 tablespoons)
  • Baking powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Vanilla extract (1/2 teaspoon)

Method

Mix all the ingredients in a bowl until you have a fairly thin batter. Heat a frying pan thoroughly, pour in a small amount of batter, and cook over medium heat. When bubbles form on the surface and no wet batter remains on top, flip the pancake and cook the other side.

Repeat with the remaining batter. Serve the pancakes with peanut or hazelnut butter, Nutella, or maple syrup.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Potato Stir-fry
item.description: Potato stir-fry with tomato recipe
item.content:encoded:
Most of us already know how to make potato stir-fry. I'll add a small twist to bring out an exceptional flavor. Let's get started.

Ingredients

  • Potato (500 grams)
  • Tomato (2)
  • Onion (1)
  • Cilantro (for serving)
  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Oil (1 tablespoon)

Method

First, peel and dice the potatoes, then rinse well. Dice 2 tomatoes into small pieces and set them aside with the potatoes. The tomato adds umami and gives the stir-fry a beautiful color.

Heat oil in a pan and add diced onion. When the onion turns lightly golden, add turmeric powder, chili powder, and salt, and stir once. Add the tomatoes and potatoes and keep stirring. Add a little water if needed and cover. The potatoes will soften and the tomatoes will break down within a few minutes. Split the green chilies and add them. Stir a couple of times and sprinkle cilantro just before serving.

This potato stir-fry is wonderful with hot paratha.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Snack Recipe: Chicken Sandwich
item.description: A chicken sandwich recipe ready in just 10 minutes
item.content:encoded:
Nothing beats a chicken sandwich for breakfast or an afternoon snack, and kids love it too. Here is a quick recipe you can make in about 10 minutes.

Ingredients

  • Boneless chicken (200 g)
  • Ginger-garlic paste (1 teaspoon)
  • Hard-boiled egg (1)
  • Carrot (1)
  • Cucumber (1 small)
  • Mayonnaise (2 tablespoons)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Black pepper powder (1 teaspoon)
  • White sandwich bread

Method

Finely grate the carrot and cucumber and squeeze out excess water. Boil the chicken with ginger-garlic paste until cooked through, about 5–7 minutes. Shred the chicken into very small pieces. Add the grated carrot and cucumber, mayonnaise, and salt. Grate in the hard-boiled egg and mix well. Season with black pepper to taste. This mixture is the sandwich filling. You can refrigerate it for up to a week.

Trim the crusts from square slices of white bread with a knife. Do not throw the crusts away — toast and grind them into breadcrumbs for later use. Spread the filling on one slice, top with another, and cut into sandwich triangles. Serve.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Butternut Squash Mash
item.description: A tasty butternut squash mash recipe
item.content:encoded:
Here is how to make a tasty butternut squash mash.

Ingredients

  • Butternut squash (250 grams)
  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Onion (1)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Cilantro (to taste)
  • Mustard oil (to taste)

Method

First, wash the butternut squash, cut it into small pieces, and boil until tender. Take off the heat and mash well.

In a bowl, mash together diced onion, diced green chilies, and chopped cilantro with salt and mustard oil. Add the mashed squash and mix until well combined.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Kholaja Pitha
item.description: A traditional Noakhali snack — kholaja pitha
item.content:encoded:
Kholaja pitha is a popular snack in the Noakhali region. It is very easy to make — here is the recipe.

Ingredients

  • Rice flour (1.5 cups)
  • Egg (1)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Oil (1 tablespoon)

Method

Mix all the dry ingredients in a bowl. Add the egg and oil. Add enough water to make a thin batter that can be spread across a pan without a spoon.

Heat a pan over high heat until very hot, then reduce the heat to medium. Pour batter into the center of the pan and swirl to coat the entire surface. This pitha cooks very quickly and does not need to be flipped. Repeat to make the rest.

Serve hot with any mash or beef curry.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Beef Tehari
item.description: An incredibly delicious beef tehari recipe
item.content:encoded:
It is hard to find anyone who does not love beef tehari. Here is how to make it quickly using Radhuni tehari mix.

Ingredients

  • Beef (1 kg)
  • Polao rice (2 cups)
  • Oil (1 cup)
  • Radhuni tehari mix (1 packet)
  • Green chilies (6–7)
  • Sour yogurt (500 g)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Onion (1 cup)
  • Cardamom (4)
  • Cinnamon (4 pieces)
  • Cloves (4)
  • Bay leaves (2)

Method

Wash the beef, cut it into small pieces, and marinate with a little oil, 1/2 kg sour yogurt, and 1 full packet of tehari mix for 30 minutes to 1 hour. In a separate pot, wash the polao rice well and drain.

In a pan, heat oil and fry most of the chopped onion until golden brown. Set half of the fried onion aside. Add half of the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaves to the remaining fried onion in the pan, then add all of the marinated beef. Cook well until tender. Beef usually takes a little longer; add water if needed. When done, set the beef aside.

In another pot, heat oil with the reserved chopped onion and the remaining whole spices. When the onion softens, add the polao rice and fry well. When the rice is toasted, add water. For 2 cups of rice, I use 6 cups of water. You can also use 5 cups water and 1 cup milk. When the rice is nearly cooked, add the prepared beef and its gravy. Stir well and cook until the water is fully absorbed. Add 6–7 whole green chilies, stir, and let it steam on dum for 10 minutes. During those 10 minutes, gently turn the tehari over 3–4 times. Finish by sprinkling fried onion over the top and serve.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Parboiled Rice Payesh
item.description: A recipe for traditional parboiled rice payesh
item.content:encoded:
Here is how to make parboiled rice payesh very easily.

Ingredients

  • Parboiled rice (1 cup)
  • Milk (1 liter)
  • Sugar (1 cup)
  • Raisins (for serving)
  • Chopped nuts (for serving)
  • Cardamom (2–3)
  • Cinnamon (2–3 sticks)
  • Cloves (2)
  • Bay leaf (1)

Method

First, wash the parboiled rice very well and drain the water. Then cook 1 cup of rice with 2 cups of water until tender and set it aside in a pot.

In a pot, combine the milk, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf, and sugar and bring it to a boil. When the sugar melts, add the cooked parboiled rice and stir gently over low heat. Keep stirring over low heat until the milk reduces and thickens. Do not stop stirring at any point, or the payesh may stick to the bottom of the pot. Finally, pour into a serving bowl and sprinkle raisins and chopped nuts on top.

item.title: Caramel Pudding
item.description: Make caramel pudding with eggs, milk, and sugar
item.content:encoded:
Pudding is one of my favorite desserts. Here is how to make caramel pudding.

Ingredients

  • Milk (1 cup / 250 ml)
  • Eggs (2)
  • Sugar (1 cup)
  • Cardamom (2)
  • Cinnamon (2 sticks)
  • Bay leaf (1)

Method

First, pour caramel into the bottom of the dish you will use for the pudding and set it aside. To make the caramel, heat 3 tablespoons of sugar and 1 tablespoon of water in a pan over low heat. Within a few minutes the water will evaporate and the mixture will turn a nut-brown color. Immediately spread it evenly across the bottom of the pudding dish. You must spread the caramel while it is still hot; once it cools it will stick to the bottom of the dish.

In another pot, heat the milk with the cardamom, cinnamon, and bay leaf. These spices remove the raw egg smell and make the pudding more flavorful. You can use vanilla extract instead if you prefer. When the milk comes to a boil, remove the pot from the heat, strain out the spices, and let the milk cool to lukewarm. It should be warm enough that you can dip a finger in and hold it there comfortably for a while. Beat the two eggs well with a whisk or fork. Then combine the eggs, milk, and remaining sugar and beat until smooth.

Pour this mixture into the pudding dish and place the dish inside a larger pot. Add water to the larger pot, making sure it comes halfway up the sides of the pudding dish. Bake in an oven preheated to 150°C for 50 minutes. You can also cook it on the stovetop over low heat if you prefer.

To check whether the pudding is done, insert a toothpick into the center and pull it out. If no wet batter clings to the toothpick, the pudding is ready. Remove it from the oven and let it cool. Finally, loosen the edges with a knife and invert it onto another dish. Cut into slices and serve.

item.title: Carrot Halwa
item.description: A recipe for my favorite snack, carrot halwa
item.content:encoded:
Carrot halwa is my favorite snack. Here is how to make it.

Ingredients

  • Carrots (1 kg)
  • Sugar (1.5 cups)
  • Ghee (2 tablespoons)
  • Chopped nuts (1 cup)
  • Milk (1 kg)
  • Raisins (for serving)
  • Pomegranate seeds (for serving)
  • Cardamom (2)
  • Cinnamon (2 sticks)
  • Bay leaf (1)

Method

First, peel the carrots, wash them well, and grate them very finely. Heat ghee in a pot and add the whole spices. When the ghee is hot, add the grated carrots and fry them well. The grated carrots will release water; keep frying until they are completely dry. Stir constantly so the carrots do not stick to the bottom of the pot. When the water has evaporated, add the sugar. The sugar will melt quickly. Then add the milk and keep stirring.

When the milk is nearly reduced, add some of the chopped nuts. Cook a little longer until the milk is completely absorbed. Remove from the heat and serve topped with the remaining chopped nuts, raisins, and pomegranate seeds.

item.title: Jorda
item.description: A recipe for jorda, a popular wedding dessert
item.content:encoded:
At weddings, jorda is my biggest attraction. Here is how to make it.

Ingredients

  • Fragrant rice (1 cup)
  • Sugar (1.5 cups)
  • Murabba (100 g)
  • Chopped nuts (for serving)
  • Raisins (to taste)
  • Rose water (1 tablespoon)
  • Food coloring (2–3 drops)
  • Orange juice (1 cup)
  • Small sweets (for serving)

Method

First, wash the rice and cook 1 cup of rice with 2 cups of water until tender. When the rice is nearly done, add 2–3 drops of orange food coloring. When the water is nearly absorbed, add the sugar, murabba, rose water, orange juice, and raisins. After stirring for a while, once all the liquid has evaporated, sprinkle chopped nuts and small sweets on top and serve.

item.title: Date Palm Jaggery Payesh
item.description: A recipe for traditional date palm jaggery payesh
item.content:encoded:
Nothing beats date palm jaggery payesh on a winter morning. Here is the recipe.

Ingredients

  • Fragrant rice (1 cup)
  • Milk (1 liter)
  • Date palm jaggery (250 g)
  • Raisins (for serving)
  • Cardamom (2–3)
  • Cinnamon (2–3 sticks)
  • Cloves (2)
  • Bay leaf (1)

Method

First, wash the fragrant rice very well and drain the water. In a pot, combine the milk, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf, and date palm jaggery and bring it to a boil. When the jaggery melts, add the fragrant rice and stir gently over low heat. The rice will cook through within a few minutes. Then keep stirring over low heat until the milk reduces and thickens. Do not stop stirring at any point, or the payesh may stick to the bottom of the pot. Finally, pour into a serving bowl and sprinkle raisins on top.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Borhani
item.description: Make refreshing borhani with yogurt, mint, and Radhuni borhani mix
item.content:encoded:
A rich meal in Bangladesh hardly feels complete without borhani. This easy version uses Radhuni borhani mix.

Ingredients

  • Radhuni borhani mix (1 packet)
  • Plain sour yogurt (1 kg)
  • Water (as needed)
  • Mint leaves (100 g)
  • Cilantro (50 g)
  • Crushed ice (as needed)
  • Green chilies (5–6)

Method

Blend the mint, green chilies, and cilantro with 1 tablespoon of water to make a paste. In a large bowl, thoroughly combine the yogurt, Radhuni borhani mix, and herb paste.

Add enough water to reach your preferred consistency. The borhani mix already contains salt, so no additional salt should be necessary. Serve with crushed ice.

Borhani can be refrigerated for up to one week.

item.title: Bottle Gourd and Prawn Curry
item.description: A simple but delicious bottle gourd and prawn curry
item.content:encoded:
When I lived in Bangladesh, bottle gourd and prawn curry was one of my favorites. Here is that recipe.

Ingredients

  • Bottle gourd (1 medium)
  • Tomato (3)
  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Onion (1)
  • Turmeric powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Prawns (20–25)
  • Salt (to taste)

Method

First, wash the bottle gourd, peel it, and cut it into small pieces. Wash the tomatoes and cut them into small pieces too. Dust the prawns with a pinch of turmeric and shallow-fry them lightly in oil. Heat oil in a pot and add chopped onion. Then add turmeric powder, chili powder, and salt. Add the bottle gourd and tomato, pour in enough water, and cover. The gourd will soften quickly. Add the fried prawns and green chilies, stir for 2–3 minutes, and serve.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Italian Pasta: Carbonara
item.description: Easily make the Italian pasta dish carbonara
item.content:encoded:
Most of us love pasta. Let's look at the traditional Italian carbonara recipe.

Ingredients

  • Spaghetti pasta (250 grams)
  • Cream (150 grams)
  • Butter (50 grams)
  • Milk (150 ml)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Black pepper powder (to taste)
  • Ham/chicken salami (200 grams)
  • Olive oil (1 tablespoon)
  • Parmesan cheese (to taste)
  • Egg yolk (1)

Method

Bring a large pot of water to a boil with 1 teaspoon of salt. Add the pasta and cook according to the time on the package—usually 10–12 minutes. Reserve some of the pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta.

In a pan, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil and add the butter. When the butter melts, add diced ham or chicken salami. Once lightly golden, add the pasta and about 100 ml of the reserved pasta water. Add the cream, milk, and salt. Cook for 1–2 minutes. Turn off the heat, add 1 egg yolk, and mix quickly. Serve with Parmesan cheese and black pepper to taste.

item.title: Beef Curry with Potato
item.description: Beef curry with potato recipe
item.content:encoded:
Most of us love beef. Here is how to make beef curry with potato.

Ingredients

  • Beef (1 kg)
  • Potatoes (4–5)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Cumin powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Coriander powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Garam masala powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Cardamom (4)
  • Cinnamon (4 pieces)
  • Cloves (4)
  • Bay leaves (2)
  • Star anise (1, optional)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Green chilies (4–5)
  • Chopped onion (1 cup)
  • Ginger paste (1 teaspoon)
  • Garlic paste (1 teaspoon)
  • Oil (1/2 cup)
  • Roasted cumin powder (1 teaspoon)

Method

Cut 1 kg of beef into medium pieces and wash well. Peel the potatoes, cut them in half, and set aside in a bowl.

Heat oil in a pot and add chopped onion. When the onion softens slightly, add all the spices one by one except green chilies and roasted cumin powder. Watch that the spices do not burn; add a little water if needed. When the masala is fried, add the beef and cook well. Beef usually takes a little longer, so keep frying it properly.

When the beef is nearly tender, add the potato pieces and water to your preferred curry consistency. Cook until both the beef and potatoes are fully done. Finish with green chilies and roasted cumin powder sprinkled over the top.

item.title: Cabbage Pakora
item.description: Make cabbage pakora easily at home
item.content:encoded:
A little fried snack in the afternoon is hard to resist. Here is a simple, tasty recipe for cabbage pakora.

Ingredients

  • Cabbage (2 cups)
  • Carrot (1)
  • Gram flour (besan) (1 cup)
  • Rice flour (1 tablespoon)
  • Egg (1)
  • Green chilies (to taste)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Cilantro (to taste)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Red chili powder (1 teaspoon)

Method

Finely shred the cabbage and toss it with 1 teaspoon salt. Let it sit for 30 minutes so the cabbage releases water. Squeeze out the moisture and transfer the cabbage to a fresh bowl. Finely chop a small carrot. Chop the green chilies and cilantro. Mix everything together with the egg and remaining spices.

This recipe uses 1 tablespoon rice flour, which makes the pakoras extra crisp after frying. Add a little water if needed to bring the mixture together. Shape into small pakoras and deep-fry over medium heat until golden brown. Drain on paper towels so excess oil is absorbed. Serve hot.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Tuna Fish Chop
item.description: An easy recipe for chop made with canned tuna
item.content:encoded:
Canned foods are everywhere in supermarkets these days. Stocking up during quarantine was the smart move — today's recipe uses that canned tuna.

Ingredients

  • Canned tuna (1 can — 190 g)
  • Mashed potato (1 cup)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Red chili powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Cumin powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Lemon juice (1 tablespoon)
  • Egg (1)
  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Cilantro (to taste)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Oil (for frying)

Method

Drain the tuna well from the can and squeeze out excess water. When buying tuna, choose tuna packed in water — oil-packed tuna does not work as well for this chop. Mix the fish with all the remaining ingredients in a large bowl. If the mixture is too stiff, add a little water. If it is too soft, add a small amount of gram flour, rice flour, or all-purpose flour. Shape into small chops and deep-fry over medium heat until golden brown. Do not fry on high heat — the outside will brown too quickly while the inside stays raw. Serve hot.

item.title: Fried Rice
item.description: Make delicious fried rice at home with ease
item.content:encoded:
Fried rice is one of my favorite dishes. Here is the recipe.

Ingredients

  • Rice (1 cup)
  • Boneless chicken (250 g)
  • Eggs (2)
  • Oil (as needed)
  • Scallion (1)
  • Green chilies (2)
  • Mushrooms (4–5)
  • Cabbage (100 g)
  • Green peas (100 g)
  • Carrot (1)
  • Cucumber (1)
  • Soy sauce (1 tablespoon)
  • A pinch of tasting salt
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Small iceberg lettuce (1)

Method

Fried rice is usually made from leftover rice. If you do not have leftover rice, cook rice with the amount listed in the ingredients, let it cool, and chill it in the refrigerator for 15 minutes.

Beat the eggs with a little salt and scramble them like scrambled eggs. Set aside in a separate bowl. Cut the chicken into small pieces, fry lightly with a little salt, and set aside.

Heat oil in a large pan and cook all the vegetables except cucumber and lettuce for a few minutes. The small-cut vegetables will become tender. Add the rice, eggs, and fried chicken. Stir in 1 tablespoon soy sauce, a pinch of tasting salt, and salt to taste. Just before serving, add the cucumber and lettuce, stir once, and serve hot.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Plain Polao
item.description: Plain white polao recipe
item.content:encoded:
No special occasion or guest meal for Bengalis is complete without polao. Here is how to make plain polao.

Ingredients

  • Chinigura polao rice (1 cup)
  • Onion (1 large)
  • Oil (as needed)
  • Cardamom (2)
  • Cinnamon (2 pieces)
  • Cloves (2)
  • Bay leaf (1)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Milk (1/2 cup)
  • Green chilies (5–6)

Method

Wash the polao rice very well and drain. Chop part of the onion and set some aside. Heat oil in a pan and fry the remaining onion until golden brown. Set the beresta aside. In the same pot, add the reserved chopped onion and whole spices. When the onion softens slightly, add the washed rice. Toast the rice over low heat. It will toast quickly. Keep hot water ready in another pot. When the rice is toasted, a wonderful aroma will rise. Add water using the rule of 3 cups water for every 1 cup of rice. Instead of 3 cups water, I use 2.5 cups water and 0.5 cup milk, which gives the polao a beautiful color.

When the water has absorbed, reduce the heat to very low and spread 5–6 whole green chilies over the top. We are using the chilies only for aroma, so do not slice them or the polao will become spicy. Bring the top layer to the bottom and the bottom layer to the top, then leave it on very low heat for 10 minutes. This is called giving it dum. During those 10 minutes, gently turn the polao over 3–4 times. Finish by sprinkling fried onion over the top and serve.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Green Mango Dal
item.description: A classic Bengali green mango dal recipe
item.content:encoded:
Green mango dal is a very popular dish. When raw mango season arrives, nothing beats a bowl of it. Here is the recipe.

Ingredients

  • Lentils (1/2 cup)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Green mango (1)
  • Onion (1)
  • Garlic (1–2 cloves)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Green chilies (1–2)
  • Cilantro (to taste)
  • Oil (2 tablespoons)

Method

In a pot, boil the washed lentils in enough water. Add 1 teaspoon of turmeric. When the lentils are cooked, season with salt and add the peeled and chopped green mango and green chilies. Take the pot off the heat once the mango softens.

Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan and fry the chopped onion and garlic until golden. Pour the oil and fried aromatics into the cooked dal. Simmer for another 1–2 minutes. Add chopped cilantro just before serving.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Mixed Vegetables
item.description: A delicious and nutritious mixed vegetable dish recipe
item.content:encoded:
We've had plenty of heavy meals — now let's turn to something healthier. Here is how to make a mixed vegetable stir-fry.

Ingredients

  • Broccoli (1 head)
  • Carrot (2)
  • Potato (1)
  • Green peas (1 cup)
  • Zucchini (1 medium)
  • Green papaya (1/2 cup)
  • Onion (1 large)
  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Turmeric powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1 teaspoon)
  • Salt (to taste)
  • Eggs (2)
  • Oil (2 tablespoons)

Method

First, wash all the vegetables and dice them into small cubes. I used what I had in the fridge — feel free to use whatever vegetables you have on hand. Drain off excess water from the vegetables. Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan and add diced onion. When the onion turns lightly golden, add turmeric and chili powder and stir. Add all the vegetables, stir well, pour in about 1 cup of water, and cover. The vegetables will cook through and the liquid will evaporate within a few minutes. Season with salt to taste. Before taking off the heat, break in the eggs and mix well, then add the green chilies. Stir for about three minutes, then remove from the heat.

Nearly every item in this dish is optional — leave out what you like. That said, eggs make the stir-fry taste exceptional, so I would not skip them.
item.author: Milon

item.title: Egg Bhuna
item.description: An easy and delicious egg bhuna recipe
item.content:encoded:
Here is a very easy and tasty egg bhuna recipe.

Ingredients

  • Eggs (3)
  • Green chilies (2–3)
  • Onions (4)
  • Turmeric powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Chili powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Ginger paste (1/2 teaspoon)
  • Garlic paste (1/4 teaspoon)
  • Salt (to taste)

Method

First, boil the eggs and peel them. Lightly score each egg a few times with a knife. Rub the eggs with a little turmeric and salt, then shallow-fry them in hot oil in a pan until golden.

In the same pan, using the remaining oil, add the chopped onions. When the onions soften, add the turmeric, chili powder, ginger paste, garlic paste, and salt. After 2–3 minutes, add a little water so the spices do not burn. Keep cooking until the masala is well fried. When it is nearly done, add the fried eggs. Just before taking the pan off the heat, add 2–3 green chilies cut into strips. Serve hot with plain white rice.
